instruction: Enable HTTPS for example.com using the Let's Encrypt certificate and key, and redirect plain HTTP to HTTPS.
Configure the Mozilla intermediate TLS profile for shop.example.com: TLS 1.2 and 1.3 with modern AEAD cipher suites.
Restrict a high-security vhost to TLS 1.3 only for secure.internal.example, pinning the TLS 1.3 cipher suites explicitly.
Enable HTTP Strict Transport Security with a one year max-age, includeSubDomains and preload for www.bank.example.
Enable OCSP stapling with the Let's Encrypt chain file for api.example.com and resolve the OCSP responder through Cloudflare DNS.
Configure a shared TLS session cache of 10 MB with a 1 day timeout and tickets disabled for all HTTPS servers on this host.
Set up a self-signed certificate for the development host dev.local in a server block listening on port 443.
Require client certificates signed by the internal CA for admin.example.com on port 443.
Enable HTTP/2 over TLS for docs.example.com using the modern http2 directive instead of the deprecated listen flag.
Serve dual RSA and ECDSA certificates on one listener so cdn.example.com works with both cipher families.
Enforce PCI DSS settings on pci.example.com: TLS 1.2 only with a strong cipher list and server cipher preference.
Disable TLS session tickets for perfect forward secrecy on pfs.example.com while keeping a shared session cache.
Run two HTTPS sites, a.example.com and b.example.com, each with its own certificate on port 443.
Use the wildcard certificate *.example.net for the www vhost and set a modern ECDH curve.
Configure nginx to use a pre-generated 4096-bit DH parameters file for the strong.example.com server block.
Configure nginx to terminate TLS for the bare IP address 203.0.113.10 that has an IP SAN certificate and no hostname.
Load an encrypted private key protected by a password file for secrets.example.com on port 443.
Enable QUIC and HTTP/3 for speed.example.com alongside TLS 1.3 and advertise HTTP/3 with an Alt-Svc header.
Create a hardened shared TLS baseline in the http block: intermediate protocols, shared session cache, tickets off and OCSP stapling on.
Set generous session resumption for m.example.com so flaky mobile clients can reuse TLS sessions for 12 hours.
